LESSON: POLITICAL DEVELOPMENT IN AFRICA

Grade: Grade 7
Subject: SOCIAL STUDIES
Strand: Political Development and Governance
Topic 5.1: Political Development in Africa
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 5

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Political Development in Africa, part of Political Development and Governance in Grade 7 SOCIAL STUDIES.

Key inquiry question: How did developments in Europe influence the scramble and partition of Africa?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. explore roles of European groups in the ‘Scramble for and Partition’ of Africa,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Political Development in Africa in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. examine the terms of the Berlin Conference of 1884- 1885 on the partitioning of Africa,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Political Development in Africa in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. illustrate the implications of colonial rule on African nations,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Political Development in Africa in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

D. advocate for elimination of neo-colonialism through good governance.

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Political Development in Africa in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

E. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. brainstorm on the terms “Scramble for and Partition of Africa and make presentations,

2. discuss the roles of European groups in the ‘Scramble for and Partition’ of Africa,

3. draw the map of Africa and indicate the areas taken up by the different European countries (Belgium, Britain, Germany, Italy, Spain, and Portugal) during the partition of Africa and display them in class,

4. using posters, display in class the terms of the Berlin conference of 1884-1885 on the partitioning of Africa.

3. draw the map of Africa and indicate the areas taken up by the different European countries (Belgium, Britain, Germany, Italy, Spain, and Portugal) during the partition of Africa and display them in class,

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Political Development in Africa together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Citizenship: learners compose songs for elimination of neo-colonialism through good governance,

● Creativity and Imagination: learners draw the map of Africa and indicate the areas taken up by the different European

countries (Belgium, Britain, Germany, Italy, Spain, and Portugal) during the partition of Africa and display them in class,

Values:
• Patriotism: Learners compose songs for elimination of neo-colonialism through good governance.

• Responsibility: learners engage in assigned roles and duties as they use posters to display in class the terms of the Berlin

conference of 1884-1885.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs)

• Inter racial-ethnic relations: Learners discuss the roles of European groups in the ‘Scramble for and Partition’ of Africa,

• Good governance: learners brainstorm on compose songs for elimination of neo-colonialism through good governance.

Link to other subjects

● Learners apply Creative Arts skills as they draw the map of Africa and indicate the areas taken up by the different European

countries during the partition of Africa.

SECTION 6: SUMMARY

Main points to remember:

1. explore roles of European groups in the ‘Scramble for and Partition’ of Africa,
2. examine the terms of the Berlin Conference of 1884- 1885 on the partitioning of Africa,
3. illustrate the implications of colonial rule on African nations,
4. advocate for elimination of neo-colonialism through good governance.

Remember the key question: How did developments in Europe influence the scramble and partition of Africa?
